findings.symptom: The linked F2 title is displayed as plain text containing raw ASCII mathematical notation (for example |delta_i| <= u, prod(1+delta_i), and gamma_d) rather than typeset notation. Neighboring formula-bearing source lines render as math. The issue is in the linked title presentation, not the F2 claim itself.
findings.mathematical_check: The visible title describes the standard product-of-1-plus-errors estimate used at source line 50. The audit checked the reference title and its use in the displayed proof; no sign, index, or inequality defect was found.
findings.suggested_repair: Retitle the cited result using concise prose or a renderer-supported math title, e.g. “A product of rounded factors differs from one by at most gamma_d.” Recheck the title against the exact statement before adopting it.

underlying_linked_title.title: If |delta_i| <= u and n u < 1, then prod (1+delta_i) = 1 + theta_n with |theta_n| <= gamma_n
underlying_linked_title.note: This referenced source is outside lane 05; this supplementary locator identifies the title text rendered from the assigned item’s line-50 reference.

diagram_candidates.claim: The age grid uses cell masses, newborn inflow F_0^k=B_h^k, interior/right fluxes F_j^k=u_j^k, and an absorbing cutoff outflow recorded in O_h.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The source specifies a spatial partition and the flux entering, crossing, and leaving it. A compact diagram can make the left renewal boundary, cell indexing, right absorbing boundary, and mass-flow signs easier to verify.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw the age axis a_0=0<...<a_J=A with cells C_j=[a_{j-1},a_j] and masses M_j^k, arrow B_h^k=F_0^k entering at a=0, rightward interior arrows F_j^k=u_j^k, and terminal arrow F_J^k leaving to cumulative outflow O_h^{k+1}=O_h^k+Δt F_J^k. Annotate the update as M_j^{k+1}=M_j^k-Δt(F_j^k-F_{j-1}^k)-Δt μ_jM_j^k; do not show any return inflow above A.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: Flux and update relations are explicit in source lines 39–43. Candidate only; no diagram is needed for the algorithm.

diagram_candidates.claim: The density has an initial-cohort branch n_0^A(a-t)S(a-t,t) for t≤a and a newborn branch B_A(t-a)S(0,a) for a<t; initial cohorts exit at cutoff A while newborn cohorts cannot reach A when T<A.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: Two characteristic branches meet at the renewal boundary and the cutoff outflow depends on which initial cohort reaches A. A time-age sketch would clarify branch domains and the absorbing boundary.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: In the (t,a) plane draw characteristics da/dt=1; mark the initial trace at t=0, newborn boundary a=0 with rate B_A(t), cutoff a=A, the split a=t, and terminal exits from initial ages x∈[A-t,A). Label survival factors S(x,t) and S(0,a) on the respective branches; do not draw newborn trajectories reaching A for t≤T<A.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: The branch formulas and outflow domain are explicit in source lines 44–54. Candidate only; the proof remains analytic.

diagram_candidates.claim: For q on the circle ||q||=ℓ with tangent momentum qᵀp=0, the pendulum multiplier follows from tangency; at bottom rest q=(0,-ℓ), λ=mg/ℓ balances gravity and acceleration is zero.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The source gives a concrete holonomic constraint, a tangent condition, gravity, a multiplier, and a distinguished equilibrium. Their geometric relation is naturally shown in a small force/constraint sketch.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw the circle ||q||=ℓ centered at the pivot, the rod vector q to the bob, gravity -mg e_2, and the constraint force -λq. At q=(0,-ℓ), show p=0 and the upward constraint force balancing downward gravity when λ=mg/ℓ. If showing a generic p, draw it tangent to the circle and label qᵀp=0.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: The equations and bottom-state signs are explicit in source lines 37–39 and checked in the screenshot. Editorial aid only.

diagram_candidates.claim: For F(x,T,μ)=0 with a one-dimensional local branch, a certified tangent τ∈ker DF drives the predictor while the supplied previous unit orientation defines a transverse section τ_kᵀ(y-z_p)=0.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The algorithm relies on tangent direction, predictor offset, a section normal, and orientation checks; a branch sketch can expose sign/orientation mismatches and distinguish the current tangent from the previous section normal.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw a local solution curve in (x,T,μ), a certified root z_p, tangent τ for the predictor step, and the transverse section hyperplane τ_kᵀ(y-z_p)=0 using the previous unit orientation τ_k as its normal. Mark the accepted corrected point at the unique local section intersection; annotate F(y)=0 on the branch and keep curve/tangent arrows consistent with the prescribed orientation.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: The maps, kernel tangent, coordinate order, section equation, and orientation convention appear explicitly at source lines 34, 36, 40, and 48. Candidate only; no diagram is required to establish correctness.

diagram_candidates.claim: A counterclockwise boundary of a strictly convex polygon has winding number 1 inside and 0 outside; along a positively oriented regular edge, the interior lies to the left and left-minus-right winding index is 1.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The proof depends on edge orientation and the left/right index jump. A diagram can make the orientation convention and the local interior/exterior side concrete, with explicit winding values.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw a strictly convex polygon with cyclically ordered vertices v_0,...,v_{m-1} and counterclockwise edge arrows. Mark an interior z with n(Γ,z)=1 and exterior q with n(Γ,q)=0. At one edge, orient its tangent in the positive real direction and label the interior locally to the left and exterior to the right, showing n_left−n_right=1.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: Orientation, winding values, and left-minus-right convention are explicit in source lines 33, 45, and 53. No existing diagram is present to contain a sign error.

existing_diagram_checks.result: No valid rendered TikZ diagram or diagram failure was recorded in the 67 assigned screenshot manifests; all 96 original-resolution tiles were reviewed. No existing diagram maps, orientations, indices, signs, or crossings required checking in this lane.

limitations: This was a local frozen-snapshot rendering review only; no HTTP/live-site review, renderer invocation, build, tests, or full mathematical audit was performed.
All item, snapshot, HTML, and PNG hashes match their recorded inputs; all listed tiles were visually opened individually.
Diagram candidates are optional editorial suggestions, not confirmed defects or repair requests.
